name: navtex
label: NAVTEX (518 kHz maritime safety)
description: NAVTEX is the international maritime safety broadcast on 518 kHz — navigational warnings, weather and SAR bulletins from coast stations on a fixed schedule. The mode is SITOR-B / NBDP: CCIR-476, 100 baud FSK, 170 Hz shift, forward-error-corrected (each char sent twice, time-diversity). High ERP MF groundwave: from the US west coast, Point Reyes (NMC) is the dominant station. On the waterfall it's two crisp lines 170 Hz apart, keying in the FEC pattern, appearing for ~10 min in NMC's scheduled slots (several/day). Decoded text streams under decoder::fldigi (vendored fldigi navtex core). MF: this preset runs the source at a low sample rate; tune dial ≈ 518 kHz − 1.5 kHz so the pair lands on the 1500 Hz sweetspot.
ai_notes: NAVTEX / SITOR-B (CCIR-476 FEC, 100 bd / 170 shift, vendored fldigi navtex core). 518 kHz international (also 490 kHz local, 4209.5 kHz). US Pacific = Point Reyes NMC, scheduled ~4-6 slots/day (not continuous — watch the waterfall for the burst). MF: source sample_rate 384 kHz, dial ≈ 516.5 kHz. mode=navtex; sitorb variant available. Strong groundwave — the realistic decodable signal on a long-wire. Output: `tail decoder --category fldigi`.
